evidence.title: Big Self-Supervised Models Advance Medical Image Classification
evidence.method: SimCLR-style pretraining on ImageNet, then continued SSL on unlabeled in-domain dermatology images (ImageNet->Derm); plus MICLe: positives built from two crops of two DIFFERENT images of the same patient case (same pathology), no labels used.
evidence.dataset: Derm: DUnlabeledDerm (unlabeled dermatology camera images; MICLe on 15,340 DTrainDerm cases, multi-image cases). Downstream: dermatology skin-condition classification (top-1 accuracy). CheXpert chest X-ray for the second task.
evidence.result: Dermatology top-1 (fine-tuning endpoint, Table 1/2/3): ImageNet->Derm ResNet-50 (4x) 63.44 (ResNet-50 1x) / 67.63 (4x) SimCLR vs 68.81 with MICLe (+1.18 pp, 4x). MICLe increments in Table 2: Derm-only RN50 4x +0.62 (66.93->67.55); ImageNet->Derm RN50 4x +1.18; Derm-only RN152 2x +0.73 (66.43->67.16); ImageNet->Derm RN152 2x +0.13 (68.30->68.43). Headline +6.7 pp top-1 is vs a SUPERVISED ImageNet baseline (63.36 -> 70.02, RN152 2x with MICLe, 1000 epochs, larger batch), not vs SimCLR. CheXpert mean AUC +1.1 pp (headline, vs supervised baseline).
evidence.mechanism: Domain-specific unlabeled data continues SSL after ImageNet init. MICLe gives more informative positives than augmentations alone when multiple images of the same case exist.
evidence.augmentation_details: Derm SimCLR: random crop with resize, color distortion strength 1.0, Gaussian blur, random flips. CheXpert best on validation: random crop, color jitter 0.5, rotation up to 45 degrees, horizontal flip; Gaussian blur DROPPED, because blur may erase texture cues tied to disease interpretation (authors' argument, not tested). Authors state comprehensive augmentation search is left to future work.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text read via saved extraction (partial: sections 3.2, 4, 5.2, Tables 1-3). Numbers verified in extracted text for Tables 1-2 and the headline text. Not a complete sequential read.
evidence.limitation: Endpoint is full fine-tuning, not a frozen linear readout. MICLe positives assume that multiple images of one patient case share one pathology. The paper does not test MICLe with a frozen-feature readout. Headline gains are vs supervised baselines, not vs strong SSL. Only 2-6 images per case used.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Directly relevant: our pool has group IDs (HAM lesion_id; PAD patient). Two transferable ideas: (a) same-group positives (E2), with a critical caveat on PAD: patient != lesion, and a patient can carry both melanoma and nevus, so same-patient positives could pull together the exact pair we need to separate. Use lesion-level groups only. (b) dermoscopy augmentation policy (E1): Azizi dropped blur for CXR, a choice that is not validated for dermoscopy.

evidence.title: Self-Supervised Pretraining Improves Self-Supervised Pretraining (Hierarchical PreTraining, HPT)
evidence.method: Initialize MoCo-v2 target-domain pretraining from an existing ImageNet MoCo-v2 model (HPT), then continue SSL on target data; variant HPT-BN re-estimates BN statistics.
evidence.dataset: 16 vision datasets incl. CheXpert (chest X-ray), Chest-X-ray-kids, BDD, RESISC, UC-Merced, Flowers, DomainNet variants, xView, VIPER, Pascal, COCO, etc.
evidence.result: HPT converged within ~5k pretraining steps for 15/16 datasets; equal or better than Base transfer or Target pretraining at 400k steps (80x longer). CheXpert and Chest-X-ray-kids: HPT matched Target pretraining in 5k steps vs 200k and 100k steps respectively (text). Overfitting after 5k steps was more pronounced on small datasets, so the authors recommend a short schedule (~5k) regardless of size. Augmentation robustness (Fig. 5): HPT stays above Target pretraining when removing ColorJitter, Grayscale, GaussianBlur, RandomHorizontalFlip one by one, but CheXpert linear performance decreases as the policy changes. Data robustness (Fig. 6): HPT gains grow as target pool shrinks (1%, 10%, 25%, 100%). HPT-BN beats Target pretraining with only 1% of images.
evidence.mechanism: Starting from a model already trained on generic data reduces the domain-gap cost; a short in-domain schedule avoids overfitting the small target pool.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text read via saved extraction (partial: Section 4.2-4.4 passages; Figs 4-6 numbers only from captions/text). Figure values not extracted.
evidence.limitation: Base model is ImageNet MoCo-v2, not DINOv2. Linear-probe numbers for CheXpert are in Fig. 4-5 only, not extracted. Our 6k-step duration and init are already in the brief's negative list (duration arm), so this evidence supports the duration result rather than proposing a new arm.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Context for E-arms: supports a short in-domain schedule (already negative in our tests). Its augmentation-robustness experiment is the only foundation-era evidence on augmentation sensitivity in a medical/continued setting, supporting the augmentation arm (E1) as a sensitivity check. Confidence: medium on direction, low on magnitude for our base.

evidence.identifier: arXiv:2102.10663 (MedAug, 2021; author list not extracted, do not cite authors from memory)
evidence.title: MedAug: Contrastive learning leveraging patient metadata improves representations for chest X-ray interpretation
evidence.method: MoCo-v2/SimCLR-style contrastive pretraining on CheXpert where positive pairs are two different images selected by patient metadata (same patient, same study, same laterality, etc.). Negatives default. Evaluation: frozen features + linear classifier ('linear fine-tuning AUC', Table 7; the same readout family as ours).
evidence.dataset: CheXpert (224,316 images, 65,240 patients); pleural effusion (main) and four other CheXpert tasks (Table 7).
evidence.result: Abstract: best criterion (same patient, same study, all lateralities) = +14.4% mean AUC vs ImageNet baseline. Table 3 (distinct-images forcing): same patient, all studies AUC 0.848 vs same patient, distinct studies 0.792. Table 6 / text: same patient + same study best, +3.4% linear AUC vs an instance-discrimination baseline (Sowrirajan 2020). Table 7 (linear AUC, Atelectasis / Cardiomegaly / Consolidation / Edema): MoCo v2 baseline 0.671 / 0.735 / 0.699 / 0.847; same patient same study 0.762 / 0.785 / 0.721 / 0.889 (i.e. +0.091 / +0.050 / +0.022 / +0.042). Using patient metadata to pick HARD NEGATIVES gave no gain over the default.
evidence.mechanism: Positives built from images with the same underlying pathology carry the disease signal. Choosing by patient alone (across studies) can hurt, because a patient's images may differ in pathology over time. Number of distinct images per query matters.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text read via saved extraction (Abstract, Sections 3-4, Tables 3-7, Discussion, Limitations, Appendix A). Partial: tables read by targeted extraction; not a complete sequential read.
evidence.limitation: CXR, not dermatology. The paper itself notes that in CheXpert any two images from the same patient AND study share the same label set; that property is what makes the positive label-consistent. Our PAD pool has patient-level IDs only, and a patient may carry melanoma and nevus. The paper's own result shows patient-only positives can hurt. Metadata-based positives also are not label-free in the strict sense of using diagnosis, but they use no diagnosis label.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Strongest evidence for E2. The readout is linear, like ours. Requires the lesion/study analogue: HAM lesion_id is the closest match to 'same patient, same study'. PAD needs a lesion or session ID, or E2 is blocked for PAD. Patient-only grouping is the paper's own failure case (Table 3).

evidence.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations (full-text passage, replaces F6 abstract-only for augmentation claims)
evidence.method: Pairwise augmentation grid on ImageNet (crop, cutout, colour distortion, Sobel, noise, blur, rotate) with linear evaluation.
evidence.result: Single transforms alone do not learn good representations. Random crop + colour distortion stands out: the paper argues cropping alone lets the net exploit colour-histogram shortcuts (Figure 6: colour histograms alone separate patches of the same image). Composing crop with colour distortion is critical. Figure 5 grid values are not reliably mapped from text extraction, so no numeric claim is made from it; the qualitative finding is the claim.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text read via saved extraction (Section 3 augmentation passages, Figures 4-6 captions and text). Figure 5 grid numbers taken from extracted text only; not verified against the figure image.
evidence.limitation: ImageNet; colour is a natural-image cue. In dermoscopy colour carries diagnosis (blue-white veil, regression) AND acquisition signal (dermoscope vs smartphone, PAD vs HAM). Colour jitter can help against device shortcuts but can also erase diagnostic colour. Both effects must be checked.
evidence.relevance_to_us: IMPORTANT FINDING for E1: our baseline augmentation is RandomResizedCrop(0.4-1) + hflip, with NO colour distortion (see brief). SimCLR's shortcut argument predicts that our pipeline can solve the contrastive task from colour statistics, which is exactly the acquisition confound the brief's NMI diagnostic tries to detect. Colour jitter is therefore the strongest reason for E1, stronger than the D4 argument alone.

experiments_ranked.name: Dermoscopy-specific augmentation policy: add D4 (rot90 + flips) and mild colour jitter; no blur
experiments_ranked.exact_change: In the SSL data transform, keep RandomResizedCrop(0.4-1) and hflip. Add random rot90 (4 orientations) with flips (D4 group, applied per view), and ColorJitter(0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.1) with p=0.8, grayscale p=0.1 is optional. Do NOT add Gaussian blur or solarize in this arm. Keep 2 views, batch 16, 6000 steps, EMA 0.99, T=0.2, same seeds 42/43/44 at 224 px.
experiments_ranked.why: NEW (full text, F19): our baseline has NO colour distortion (RRC + hflip only). SimCLR shows crop-only views can be solved via colour-histogram shortcuts, and colour distortion is critical to remove them. Our PAD vs HAM acquisition difference is a colour/device shortcut risk, so colour jitter is the main reason for this arm. Dermoscopy also has no canonical orientation, and the brief shows D4 test-time augmentation already reduced HAM mel->NV from 24.4% to 19.7%. Training with the same invariance could make it a representation property rather than a readout trick. Azizi used colour jitter 0.5 and rotation for CXR, and dropped blur because it can erase disease texture (Azizi, F1). Reed reports HPT robustness to removing augmentations but a measurable CheXpert decrease, so augmentation choice is a real sensitivity (F2).
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Subjective: ~35% chance of a seed-consistent gain (>=1 pp) on HAM mel recall or PAD SCC recall with macro-F1 non-decreasing. Largest chance of effect is on mel->NV because it matches the TTA mechanism. Risk of no change ~50%.
experiments_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_6k_run: ~1.0x. Same number of forward/backward passes; augmentation is CPU-side. Three seeds x one run each = same as a baseline arm.
experiments_ranked.risk: Colour jitter may change lesion colour cues (blue-white veil, regression) that matter for melanoma. Mitigation: a colour-off sub-arm (rotation-only) run as a control. Also D4 may pull together flipped-but-different lesion structures if orientation carries signal (low probability).
experiments_ranked.excluded_because: Augmentation policy is not in the brief's negative list.
evidence: F1 (Azizi: colour 0.5, rotation, no blur for CXR; full text partial)
F2 (Reed: augmentation robustness, full text partial)
F6 (SimCLR: augmentation composition critical, abstract only)

experiments_ranked.name: Same-lesion positives (MICLe-style) as an additional positive-pair source
experiments_ranked.exact_change: With probability p=0.3 per anchor, draw view B from a different image of the SAME lesion group (HAM lesion_id; PAD lesion-level ID if available) instead of a second crop of the same image; keep the MoCo loss and in-batch negatives unchanged. Skip PAD anchors whose group is patient-level only. Log the fraction of group-positive pairs per batch and whether any pair crosses a lesion-diagnosis boundary (diagnosis is used ONLY for this audit, never in the loss).
experiments_ranked.why: Second pass: MedAug (F18, full text) is the closest evidence. Same-patient-AND-same-study positives improved frozen linear AUC over MoCo v2 on CheXpert (+0.022 to +0.091 across four findings), with a linear readout like ours. Azizi's MICLe (F1) gave +0.62 to +1.18 pp for dermatology fine-tuning. Both show the same principle: positives must share the pathology. HAM lesion_id is the closest analogue to 'same study'. PAD patient-only grouping is the failure case MedAug reports (Table 3: same patient, distinct studies 0.792 vs 0.848).
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Subjective, revised after MedAug: ~30% chance of a seed-consistent gain in HAM mel recall with macro-F1 non-decreasing (HAM lesion_id only). ~10% chance of a useful effect on PAD with patient-only grouping (MedAug suggests it may hurt). Frozen-readout gains on CXR were larger than dermatology fine-tuning gains, but CXR labels are constant within patient+study by construction; in HAM, lesion-level diagnosis is also constant within lesion_id, which is the analogous property to check.
experiments_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_6k_run: ~1.0x compute; extra image loads from the same group. Memory unchanged.
experiments_ranked.risk: HIGH on PAD if IDs are patient-level: one patient can carry melanoma and nevus, so same-patient positives may pull the exact pair (MEL vs NEV) together. The arm is only valid where group = one lesion. Requires an offline check of group purity before running. Also SSL on group IDs is label-free but uses metadata, so state this in Track A reporting.
experiments_ranked.excluded_because: Positive-pair construction is not in the brief's negative list; the brief's sampler audit (0.49%) concerns negatives, not positives.
evidence: F1 (Azizi: MICLe, Table 2, full text partial)

experiments_ranked.name: MoCo-v2 style key queue (K=4096) to decouple negatives from batch 16
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Add a FIFO queue of 4096 L2-normalised key projections from the EMA teacher (momentum 0.99 unchanged). Logits per anchor = 1 positive + 4096 queue negatives + in-batch negatives optional. Temperature T=0.2 unchanged. Queue refreshed each step with the current batch keys. Keep 2 views, batch 16, 6000 steps.
experiments_ranked.why: Batch 16 gives only 15 in-batch negatives. SimCLR and the MI analysis report that negative count and hardness matter (F6, F11). MoCo's queue is the standard way to add negatives without batch size (F12). This is the only negatives-count arm in the list; the brief does not test queue size.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Subjective: ~30% chance of a clearer representation (linear readout, seed-consistent) with macro-F1 non-decreasing. Risk that stale keys hurt: ~25%.
experiments_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_6k_run: ~1.0x compute (keys already computed by the EMA teacher). Memory: 4096 x D floats, negligible. Confound: with a queue, the effective temperature/momentum interaction may shift, so run the baseline in the same environment.
experiments_ranked.risk: Stale queue with momentum 0.99 at 6000 steps (queue covers ~256 steps at batch 16). Could reduce separability if queue keys come from an earlier, different encoder state. Also changes what 'in-batch' means in the logs.
experiments_ranked.excluded_because: Queue size is not in the brief's negative list; momentum and temperature are, but the queue is a different mechanism.
evidence: F6 (SimCLR: batch and negative sensitivity, abstract only)
F11 (MI view: negative choice critical, abstract only)

experiments_ranked.name: Multi-crop local views (2 global at 224 + 2-4 local at 98 px, scale 0.05-0.4)
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Add 2 local crops at 98 px (scale 0.05-0.4) per image to the 2 global views. Loss: each local view predicts the EMA teacher's global-view distribution (SwAV/DINO-style cross-view), with the InfoNCE pipeline unchanged in form. Batch 16, 6000 steps.
experiments_ranked.why: Multi-crop is a classic gain for local-global correspondence (F4, F8). It may help lesion-border and texture cues that separate SCC vs BCC or MEL vs NEV at local scale.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Subjective: ~20% chance of a seed-consistent gain on SCC recall or PAD MEL recall; ~40% chance of no change. DINOv2 already uses multi-crop in its own pretraining, so a further gain is uncertain.
experiments_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_6k_run: ~1.15-1.25x (INFERENCIA, our arithmetic): 2 local crops at 98 px = 2 x 49 tokens vs 2 global views at 224 px = 2 x 256 tokens, so about +19% tokens; attention cost is lower for the locals. Verify with a timed 50-step run before scheduling.
experiments_ranked.risk: Redundancy with DINOv2's pretraining. Local crops at 98 px may be too small for dermoscopy structure at the chosen resolution. The loss change is not a pure sampler change, so it needs a new code path and a unit test for the loss.
experiments_ranked.excluded_because: Multi-crop is not in the brief's negative list, but the brief's 448 px and patch-pooling arms touch resolution and local features, so check for overlap with the 224 patch-pooling negative result before running.
evidence: F8 (SwAV abstract: multi-crop at similar cost)
F10 (DenseCL: local-level gains, dense tasks only)

experiments_ranked.name: Stronger-augmentation auxiliary branch (CLSA-lite)
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Add a third view with strong augmentation (colour jitter 0.8, Gaussian blur, solarize p=0.2, rotation D4) and align its embedding to the weak-view teacher's distribution over a representation bank (CLSA's divergence term), leaving the MoCo loss on the two weak views unchanged.
experiments_ranked.why: CLSA reports gains from strong augmentations only when a distribution-divergence term supervises them (F14). Strong views may force invariance to acquisition colour (phase, device) that confounds the readout.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Subjective: ~15% chance of a clear macro-F1 gain; largest risk of harm. Lowest priority.
experiments_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_6k_run: ~1.4-1.5x (INFERENCIA): one extra full-resolution view plus a bank. Estimated from forward passes, not timed.
experiments_ranked.risk: High: CLSA's abstract says naive strong augmentation alone does not learn well, and our pool is small (12 + 4 images per step). Bank size and divergence temperature add hyperparameters, which the brief has already flagged as costly. Blur conflicts with E1's no-blur choice, so run E5 only if E1 shows an augmentation effect.
experiments_ranked.excluded_because: Not in the brief's negative list; but it depends on E1 and is the most expensive.

recommended_order: E1 first: cheapest (~1.0x), not in brief's negative list, grounded in full-text derm/medical evidence and in our own D4 TTA result.
E3 second: cheap (~1.0x), tests the negatives count that the brief never varied. Run with baseline refit in the same environment.
E2 only after an offline group-purity audit (lesion-level IDs on both HAM and PAD). Without that audit, skip the PAD part.
E4 only after a timed 50-step benchmark and an overlap check with the 224 patch-pooling result.
E5 only if E1 shows an augmentation effect; highest cost and risk.
common_caveats: All numbers from F1 and F2 were extracted from full-text pages by targeted search, not a sequential full read. Figure values (Reed Figs 4-6) were not extracted.
Abstract-only items (F3-F17) are not quoted for numbers beyond their abstract statements.
Expected-effect percentages are subjective priors (INFERENCIA), not measured values. Compute ratios for E4 and E5 are estimates.
No experiment was run; no file other than this JSON was written. Temporary extraction files are in /tmp/ssl-foundations-papers/ (not in the repo).
Track A reporting: E2 uses group metadata (patient or lesion IDs) as positives. This is label-free regarding diagnosis, but it is metadata-based, so flag it explicitly.
gaps: No dermatology paper with a frozen-readout evaluation of augmentation or MICLe-style positives on melanoma vs nevus or SCC vs BCC was found in the 14 searches.
arXiv search returned nothing in the prior run; the arXiv route was used only for full-text reads of IDs found through OpenAlex.
Queue-size, batch-size and multi-crop effects for medical or dermoscopy SSL were not found with numbers in the abstracts retrieved.
Lesion-level vs patient-level group IDs for PAD were not verified in this reviewer's scope; this is a data check that must happen before E2.
